html:
In 1893, after the Franco-Siamese crisis, Siam gave up the lands east of the Mekong to France. They became the protectorate of Laos, part of French Indochina.

France joined the old Lao kingdoms into one territory, keeping the king of Luang Phrabang and ruling the rest directly from Vientiane. It invested little: Laos had few roads and schools, and many officials were Vietnamese.

The Mekong became a border, leaving most Lao speakers in Siam. The Lao Issara movement declared independence in 1945, and France granted full sovereignty in 1953, just before the war in Indochina ended. Laos then slid into the Laotian Civil War.
